sentences.text:
The DAR revealed that a Road Traffic Accident took place on 22.10.2021 at about 6:00 P.M. at New Rohtak Road, Liberty Cinema Red Light, Karol Bagh,
Delhi wherein the petitioner Prem Yash Rai had sustained grievous injury.
The accident took place with the vehicle i.e. Champion bearing registration No. DL 1CN 4059 driven by respondent no.1 Sh. Fakir Singh and owned by respondent no.2 Sh. Phool Singh.
The said vehicle was not insured.

BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE:
2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on on 22.10.2021 on receiving DD No.
74A, SI Murari Lal along with staff reached at New Rohtak Road Liberty Cinema Red Light where accidental scooty was found parked along the roadside and eye witness Akshay Sethi had met them.
The injured had already been taken to RML Hospital by PCR Van.
The IO went to RML Hospital where the injured was found under treatment vide MLC No. E/228572/21 and the doctor had stated that the patient was not fit for statement.

The IO returned at the spot where the eye witness namely Sh. Akshay was found and IO recorded his statement wherein he stated that on 22.10.2021 when he was going to Mangolpuri Market from his work place at Paharganj, at about 6.00 P.M. and when he stopped at red light of Liberty Cinema at New Rohtak Road, he saw that on his opposite side, one green coloured Champion came from the side of Anand Parbat in a very high speed while driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the scooty due to which, the rider of the scooty fell down along with his scooty.

The witness also stated that many public persons had gathered at the spot and the driver of the offending vehicle tried to run from there but he followed him and stopped him at Ramjas Road red light and clicked the photograph of the said vehicle and also made video of the driver and vehicle.
He returned to the spot and called at 100 number.
The police came and took the injured to RML Hospital.
Since the injured was not able to make his statement, the FIR was registered on the statement of the eye-witness.
During the course of investigation, the IO had arrested the driver of the vehicle.
3. During the course of investigation, the IO prepared the site plan of the place of accident.
The IO investigated about the offending vehicle and came to know that the said vehicle was in the name of one Sh. Phool Singh who was served with the notice under section 133 M.V. Act.
The owner stated that at the time of the accident, Fakir Chand was driving the vehicle and he produced the offending vehicle and the driver at the police station.

The driver admitted his guilt and on enquiry, he disclosed that he was driving the said vehicle without a valid driving licence and insurance and therefore, he was also chargesheeted under section 5/181 M.V. Act.
The driver of the offending vehicle Fakir Chand was arrested and since the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds.
During further investigation, the offending vehicle was seized by the IO and sent to Malkhana.
The offending vehicle did not have valid insurance policy.
4. The offending vehicle was sent for mechanical inspection.
The IO had collected the MLC of the injured after final opinion and the injury was shown as 'grievous' on the MLC of the petitioner and therefore, section 338 of IPC was added.
On completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC and section 5/181 MV Act was filed against the driver Fakir Chand and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 16.04.2022.

7. The Petitioner filed the Form XIV.

FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS
8. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the petitioner and Ld. Counsels for the respondents and carefully perused the record.

My findings on the various issues are as under:-
9.

Before delving into the facts of the current case to decide the aforementioned issues, it is pertinent to highlight that it is firmly established in legal precedents that the proceedings conducted before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of an inquiry.

Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287).

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation.

In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.

sentences.text: 10. Keeping in mind the aforementioned legal principle for adjudicating the present issue, this Tribunal has thoroughly gone through the testimony of the witnesses and all the material available on record.
Also, careful consideration has been given to the arguments addressed by the Learned Counsels for all the parties.

The factum of accident:

12. PW-1, Mr. Prem Yash Rai, has proved the factum of the accident and the identity of the respondent no.1.

He has unequivocally testified that respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1LN-4059, which was coming from back side i.e. Anand Parbat side without following the traffic rules, norms and rashly, negligently and carelessly and hit the vehicle of the injured from the back side.

The deposition of PW-1 as to the manner of the accident and the driving of the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner by the respondent no. 1 remained unshaken during cross-examination of the said witness and in fact was strengthened during the same.

13. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the respondents argued that there is no eye witness to the accident and even the petitioner has admitted that he does not know the particulars of the offending vehicle.

However, from the testimony of PW-1 and entire record, it stands proved that respondent no.1 acted in a rash and negligent manner while driving his vehicle due to which the petitioner suffered grievous injuries.
In fact, in the cross-examination of PW-1, Ld. Counsel for the respondents asked a suggestion to which PW-1 replied that "It is correct that the offending vehicle hit my scooty from the back."
This implies that the accident is admitted on the part of the respondents.
14. PW-1 Prem Yash Rai has specifically deposed qua the driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1LN-4059 by respondent no. 1 in a reckless, rash and negligent manner.

Also,
the respondents did not file any written statement or led any evidence in their defence nor respondent no.1 himself appeared in the witness box and as such adverse inference has to be drawn against them.

The injury:
16.

The petitioner (PW-1) testified that due to the accident, he sustained grievous head injuries and right side parental bone fractures and left temporal, left side subdineal hemorrhage and other multiple injuries all over his body.

He asserted that upon the accident, he was taken to RML Hospital and his treatment took place w.e.f. 22.10.2021 to 23.10.2021.
17.

From the above deposition and in totality of the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to bring on record sufficient facts so as to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number DL-1LN-4059 by its driver/respondent no.
1 on the date and time of the accident and that due to the said accident, the petitioner had suffered grievous injury.

Compensation:
18.
The petitioner is certainly entitled for compensation in view of decision of the discussion on the above issues.

Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases.

In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.

sentences.text:
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv).
19.

In view of the above law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in injury cases, award needs to be passed only under heads of medical expenses, loss of earning during treatment period and damages for pain, suffering and trauma.
This Tribunal now proceeds further step by step to decide the compensation/award under different heads applicable to the present matter in light of above preposition.

Thus, his compensation is computed as follows:
Medical expenses:
21.
The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- with respect to medical expenses in his Form XIV.
However, he has not filed any medical bill on record to prove the same.
The petitioner, as PW-1, has even admitted in his cross-examination that "It is correct that I have not placed on record any medical bill.
"However, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner must have incurred some expense on his medical treatment.

Therefore, the petitioner/ injured shall be entitled to Rs.5,000/- as notional expense towards medical expenses.
Loss of income:
22.

Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Prem Yash Rai claimed that he was a shopkeeper at the time of the accident and was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month, but due to the accident in question he has not able to work.
However, the petitioner has not filed any document to show that he was a shopkeeper or that he was earning Rs.20,000 /- per month.
Thus, the income of the petitioner will have to be assessed as per the minimum wages.
The petitioner has filed on record his Aadhar card bearing no. 7340 3050 5167 as per which he was a resident of Delhi.
Thus, it is proved that he was a resident of Delhi, however, no educational qualification or special skill has been placed on record.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of employment and income and considering his address to be of Delhi, the minimum wages for an unskilled labour prevalent in Delhi at the time of the accident (on 22.10.2021) i.e. Rs.16,064/- is taken as the income of the petitioner/ injured Prem Yash Rai.
Therefore, it is held that the monthly income of the petitioner/ injured Prem Yash Rai at the time of the accident i.e. on 22.10.2021 was Rs.16,064/-.
Further, the petitioner has claimed that he has not been able to work since the accident but there is no proof of the same.
However, keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to the Loss of Income for 03 months i.e. Rs.16,064/- x 3 = Rs. 48,192/-.

Pain and Suffering:
23.
The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 20,000/- under the head pain and suffering, however, no justification has been given for claiming such a huge amount.
It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies from case to case.
Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received grievous injuries,
therefore
, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner as mentioned in the MLC, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs. 10,000/-
towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.facts:
During the course of investigation, the IO had arrested the driver of the vehicle.
The IO investigated about the offending vehicle and came to know that the said vehicle was in the name of one Sh. Phool Singh who was served with the notice under section 133 M.V. Act.
The owner stated that at the time of the accident, Fakir Chand was driving the vehicle and he produced the offending vehicle and the driver at the police station.
The driver admitted his guilt and on enquiry, he disclosed that he was driving the said vehicle without a valid driving licence and insurance and therefore, he was also chargesheeted under section 5/181 M.V. Act.
The driver of the offending vehicle Fakir Chand was arrested and since the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds.
During further investigation, the offending vehicle was seized by the IO and sent to Malkhana.
The offending vehicle did not have valid insurance policy.
4. The offending vehicle was sent for mechanical inspection.
The IO had collected the MLC of the injured after final opinion and the injury was shown as 'grievous' on the MLC of the petitioner and therefore, section 338 of IPC was added.
On completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC and section 5/181 MV Act was filed against the driver Fakir Chand and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 16.04.2022.
The petitioner closed his evidence.
After the said accident the deponent fell down on the road with e- scooty and received head grievous injuries and right side parental bone fractures and left temperal, left side subdineal hemorrhage and other multiple injuries all over his body.
The injured/petitioner was taken to RML Hospital, Delhi for treatment where he was admitted and thereafter treated by the doctors and admitted since 22.10.2021 and discharged on 23.10.2021 and the treatment is still continuing.
The accident was caused due to careless driving/act on the pat of the respondent no. 1.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287).
In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation.
In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.
From the above deposition and in totality of the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to bring on record sufficient facts so as to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number DL-1LN-4059 by its driver/respondent no.
1 on the date and time of the accident and that due to the said accident, the petitioner had suffered grievous injury.
The petitioner is certainly entitled for compensation in view of decision of the discussion on the above issues.
In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4.
(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.

The petitioner has filed his medical record to prove his nature of injuries as per which, injured has suffered grievous injuries in the incident in question.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of employment and income and considering his address to be of Delhi, the minimum wages for an unskilled labour prevalent in Delhi at the time of the accident (on 22.10.2021) i.e. Rs.16,064/- is taken as the income of the petitioner/ injured Prem Yash Rai.
, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries.
In the case of Benson George v Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. in Civil Appeal No. 1540 of 2022 decided on 25.02.2022, Hon'ble Supreme Court had awarded an interest of 6% per annum.
